dedupe_keys.name: repair methods and costs for earthquake damaged building components in new zealand

description: Repair methods and costs for earthquake-damaged building components in New Zealand is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Timothy Sullivan, University of Canterbury (canterbury.ac.nz). The University of Canterbury and industry affiliates have collaborated to develop repair costs for earthquake-damaged building components in New Zealand, current in 2021. The deliverables for this project have been provided electronically and comprise two Excel spreadsheets and a PDF: "NZrepairtime&costmaster20210119.csv" provides a summary of component damage states, repair methods, repair costs, and repair time. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-c9kw-n302. Keywords: Loss assessment, Repair methods, Repair costs, Repair time. Published 2021-05-25. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
